article_lead.description: the part of EM that uses a current model to assign probabilities to missing labels, making a difficult likelihood easier to fit

new_bank_questions.title: Which parameter supplies E-step weights?
new_bank_questions.body: In Q(Psi;Psi_old), which argument determines the conditional distribution of the missing labels, and which is optimized in the M step?
new_bank_questions.answer: Psi_old fixes the conditional distribution and therefore all E-step responsibilities. The candidate Psi is varied in the M step while those responsibilities stay fixed.

new_bank_questions.title: Equal component densities
new_bank_questions.body: Two mixture components have equal density at x, but current weights 0.8 and 0.2. Find the E-step responsibility of the first component.
new_bank_questions.answer: It is 0.8: Bayes' numerator multiplies each density by its current mixture weight, and the equal densities cancel.

new_bank_questions.title: A symmetric normal-mixture E step
new_bank_questions.body: Two unit-variance normal components have equal current weights and means 0 and 2. Find the responsibility for the first component at x=1.
new_bank_questions.answer: Both weighted densities agree at the midpoint, so the responsibility is 1/2. This is conditional uncertainty, not an observed class label.
